Abraham's wisdom deep in his kidneys ('yo'atzot oto u-melamdot oto chochmah') is a Torah of chesed that Eliezer drew out for others. The maamar pairs 'kelayot yo'atzot' with the Oral Torah as 'Torat chesed' taught to students.

found.why: 'Zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah' read as wisdom rooted above, and 'ba ba-yamim' as entering the inner light of the days. This is the maamar's pairing of zaken = acquired wisdom with 'ba ba-yamim' as the supernal days.

found.ref: Beit Aharon, Teachings on Torah and Holidays, R' Aharon (the Second) of Karlin, Genesis, Chayei Sara 3
found.why: Abraham's 'zaken' is the wisdom he acquired, 'ba ba-yamim' is binding all his middot to that wisdom, and only then 'Bakol' ('bat … u-Vakol shemah'). This is the maamar's order exactly: zaken = kanah chochmah, refined in all the middot, then 'blessed in all'.

Reads 'zaken ba ba-yamim' as Abraham being raised to the upper world, and 'bat … u-Vakol shemah' as the receiving lower realm (a 'midah u-mekabel') made fit for blessing. This is close to the maamar's 'Bakol' = Malchut after 'yomin ila'in'.

'Zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah' with 'bi-yeshishim chochmah': wisdom that has settled and is fixed (be-kevi'ut), with all the days whole. This matches the maamar's wisdom 'engraved on the heart permanently' and 'full of days'.

footnotes.text:
**Ohr HaTzafun, Bereshit, XVI 8-10** (Mussar) — On Shabbat 56b, the Alter of Slabodka holds that Solomon did not actually go after other gods. Even so, an inclination of heart too fine to be noticed is enough for Scripture to say "his heart was not whole." This fits Rav Tzadok's Solomon, whose heart was turned before he sensed it.
שבשמים רואים בזה לבד שנשיו בקשו להטותו איזו נטיה בתוך לבו לאלהים אחרים

**Ohr HaTzafun, Bereshit, XIX 6-9** (Mussar) — Abraham's wisdom lay deep in his kidneys, which "counselled and taught him wisdom." That wisdom was a Torah of chesed, which Eliezer drew out and gave to others. Compare Rav Tzadok's link between "the kidneys counsel" and the Oral Torah as "a Torah of kindness" taught to students.
חכמתו של אברהם היתה עמוקה בתוך כליותיו

**Sefat Emet, Genesis, Chayei Sara 31:3** (Chassidus) — The Sefat Emet reads "zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah" as wisdom of one's root above. He reads "ba ba-yamim" as entering the inner light hidden in each day. Rav Tzadok makes the same pairing: zaken as acquired wisdom, and "advanced in days" as the supernal days.
ופי' בא בימים בפנימיות הימים

footnotes.ref: Beit Aharon, Teachings on Torah and Holidays, R' Aharon (the Second) of Karlin, Genesis, Chayei Sara 3
footnotes.text:
**Beit Aharon, Chayei Sara 3** (Chassidus) — R. Aharon of Karlin reads the verse in three steps. "Zaken" is the wisdom Abraham acquired, "ba ba-yamim" is binding all his middot to it, and then comes "blessed in all" ("bat … u-Vakol shemah"). This is the order of Rav Tzadok's reading: acquired wisdom, refinement in all the middot, then "Bakol."
לזה כתיב מקודם ואברהם זקן היינו החכמה ואחר כך בא בימים אלו המדות

**Sefat Emet, Genesis, Chayei Sara 24:3** (Chassidus) — The Sefat Emet holds that all agree "zaken ba ba-yamim" means Abraham was raised to the upper world. The view that he had a daughter named Bakol means the receiving, lower realm (the "bat," a vessel) was also made fit to hold the blessing. Compare Rav Tzadok's reading of "Bakol" as Malchut, which comes after the "supernal days."
לכן יש אומרים אפילו ברתא לא חסרי' רחמנא שהי' לו בחי' בת ובכל שמה

**Torah Ohr, Mishpatim 7:16** (Chassidus) — The Alter Rebbe reads "zaken zeh she-kanah chochmah" together with "bi-yeshishim chochmah." The elder's wisdom is settled and fixed, with all his days whole. Compare Rav Tzadok's "zeh": wisdom engraved on the heart permanently.
דהיינו שתהיה עבודה בקביעות ובישוב הדעת ולא יהיה פעם כך ופעם כך
